To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the variational auto-encoder is a point in a space of trade-offs, and that it is possible to find other points in this space with similar generative performance that make different trade-offs.

the standard evidence lower-bound objective is insufficient to choose among points on the optimal frontier, that targeted optimization to learn models at different points along the optimal frontier is possible, and that our framework sheds light onto the design space of latent-variable models.

the variational auto-encoder is an efficient model that can learn a good representation, but it can be improved in terms of both the representation and the generative model by making different trade-offs in the rate-distortion plane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: What is the best way to use the latent space?
understanding and controlling the trade-offs between generative performance, communication cost, and the usage of latent variables in deep latent-variable models.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our framework provides an information-theoretically principled framework for understanding tradeoffs in unsupervised latent-variable learning.
the variational auto-encoder is a good starting point but it is not optimal in terms of the trade-off between the reconstruction error (rate) and the latent space (distortion) that it achieves.
the proposed approach is a novel way to analyze and understand trade-offs in unsuervised learning of deep generative models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new way to think about unsupervised learning with latent variables.
, in order to understand the performance of a variational autoencoder, we need to consider the rate and distortion of the latent variables.
the standard ELBO objective is a good proxy for the distortion of generative models, but not for its rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in addition to the standard distortion metric, we must carefully consider the cost of communicating the latent variables when evaluating the performance of a generative model.
the choice of generative model is not only a trade-off between reconstruction and communication, but also a choice between the amount of information that can be extracted from the data.
the choice of the rate-distortion frontier is a fundamental aspect of generative models, and we must be explicit in choosing this frontier when evaluating and comparing generative models.
